statement.document_title: NVIDIA Isn't Enron - So What Is It?

from_speaker: AI agents are a pipedream and simply do not work
the cost of inference ... keeps going up
our_interpretation: Assess the sentence as a bundle of contemporary empirical assertions, rather than treating its rhetorical phrases as separate forecasts.
Use empirical observations from 2025 completed before the post. Unlike financial reporting, these evaluations have no common quarterly reporting period.

Read agents do not work as a broad denial that agents can successfully perform useful delegated tasks. Repeated success on bounded tasks counts against that denial, without establishing dependable autonomous employees.
Read developer slowdown as a general productivity claim measured by completion time at comparable quality. A study of one setting supports only that setting.
Read rising inference cost as increasing cost to obtain comparable output or performance. Total industry spending and spending on increasingly capable models are separate measures.
Limited and unreliable lack numerical thresholds; assess documented failures and reliability limits without inventing a universal acceptable failure rate.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled studies show developer slowdown and evaluations show material reliability limits. Full support would additionally require representative evidence for broad agent failure and rising comparable-workload inference costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Repeated agent task success contradicts the categorical agent assertion; representative productivity gains contradict general slowdown; declining comparable-performance inference prices contradict the unit-cost reading. A mixed outcome requires evidence for identifiable supporting and opposing parts.

evidence.locator: Opening summary; methodology and Core Result
evidence.explanation: The February–June experiment found slowdown among 16 experienced developers completing 246 tasks in familiar open-source repositories. It supports that setting, and the authors explicitly reject generalizing it to most software development.

Agents successfully completed a measurable share of multi-step software and reasoning tasks, contradicting a categorical denial of task-level usefulness. A 50% success threshold also leaves substantial reliability limitations and does not establish dependable autonomous employment.

The analysis through November 2025 finds falling prices at fixed benchmark performance, opposing the comparable-output reading. It also reports that benchmark-running costs can remain flat or rise as models pursue higher performance, so it does not establish falling total spending or provider production costs.

evidence.locator: Opening results discussion, before Wider adoption
evidence.explanation: The follow-up begun in August 2025 produced point estimates favoring speedup, but confidence intervals included no effect and selection problems weakened inference. Its window is not isolated to the pre-publication period, so it limits extrapolation from the earlier study rather than deciding the December claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative pre-publication deployment and productivity studies, plus a specified inference-cost measure, would settle the remaining broad assertions.
